hello.note: Works at any time of day, often with palms pressed together. नमस्ते (namaste) is also used.

goodbye.note: Lit. 'I'll come (again)': Marathi avoids saying 'I'm going'. A woman says: येते (yete).

please.note: Formal. In speech, politeness comes from the verb form or a soft ना: बसा ना (basa na).

thank_you.note: More formal: मी आभारी आहे (mi aabhaari aahe). Many people simply say थँक यू (thank you).

youre_welcome.note: Marathi has no set reply to thanks; this ('oh, it's nothing') is the natural one.

yes.note: Also होय (hoy), the fuller form: a little more formal, and the one used in writing.

no.note: To turn down an offer, say नको (nako), 'I don't want it'.

excuse_me.note: People also call strangers दादा (daada, 'brother') or ताई (taai, 'sister'). In cities: एक्सक्यूज मी (excuse me).

good_morning.note: Formal or in messages. Face to face, most people say नमस्कार (namaskaar) or गुड मॉर्निंग (good morning).

how_are_you.note: To a woman: तुम्ही कशा आहात? (tumhi kasha aahat?). Casual: कसं काय? (kasa kaay?)

im_fine.note: A woman says: मी बरी आहे (mi bari aahe). Also common: मी मजेत आहे (mi majet aahe).

whats_your_name.note: More formal: आपलं नाव काय? (aapla naav kaay?)

my_name_is.note: The verb आहे (aahe, 'is') comes last, after the name.

where_from.note: To a woman: तुम्ही कुठल्या आहात? (tumhi kuthlya aahat?)

im_from.note: A woman says: मी …ची आहे (mi …chi aahe). The place name changes form: पुणे → पुण्याचा (Pune → Punyaacha).

speak_english.note: Lit. 'Does English come to you?' Many say इंग्लिश (English) instead of इंग्रजी.

dont_understand.note: Also common: मला कळलं नाही (mala kalla naahi).

speak_slowly.note: More direct: कृपया हळू बोला (krupaya halu bola).

what.note: To ask someone to repeat, politer: काय म्हणालात? (kaay mhanaalaat?)

why.note: The same word ends yes/no questions: येतं का? (yeta ka?). Also common: कशाला? (kashaala?, 'what for?')

how_much.note: For the total at the till: किती झाले? (kiti jhaale?)

where_bathroom.note: Also common: बाथरूम (bathroom). Signs say स्वच्छतागृह (swachchhataagruh) or शौचालय (shauchaalay).

what_time.note: The answer uses the same verb: दोन वाजले (don vaajle), 'it's two o'clock'.

four.note: Marathi digit: ४. Here च sounds like 'ts': tsaar.

five.note: Marathi digit: ५. The final च sounds like 'ts': paats.

eight.note: Marathi digit: ८. ठ is a tongue-curled t with a puff of air, not English 'th'.

water.note: ण is a retroflex n: curl the tongue back to say it.

tea.note: Here च sounds like 'ts': tsaha. It comes with milk and sugar unless you ask otherwise.

bread.note: Soft bread rolls, as in वडापाव (vadapaav). Sliced bread: ब्रेड (bread). Flatbread: पोळी (poli).

menu_please.note: जरा (jara, 'a little') softens a request, much like 'please'.

delicious.note: Said of food that has 'turned out' well. Casual: एकदम मस्त! (ekdam mast!) The word for tasty: चविष्ट (chavisht).

no_meat.note: Also: मी शाकाहारी आहे (mi shaakaahaari aahe), 'I'm vegetarian'.

enjoy_meal.note: Marathi has no fixed 'bon appétit'; hosts say this, lit. 'eat unhurriedly'.

left.note: Turn left: डावीकडे वळा (daavikade vala). Drivers also say लेफ्ट (left).

right.note: Turn right: उजवीकडे वळा (ujvikade vala). Drivers also say राइट (right).

stop_here.note: Softer, to a driver: दादा, इथे थांबवा ना (daada, ithe thaambva na).

airport.note: In everyday speech most people say एअरपोर्ट (airport).

hotel.note: In Maharashtra हॉटेल often means a restaurant or eatery, too.

train_station.note: Often just स्टेशन (station). Signs say रेल्वे स्थानक (railway sthaanak).

want_to_go.note: The place takes -ला ('to'): मला पुण्याला जायचं आहे (mala Punyaala jaaycha aahe).

is_it_far.note: How far is it? किती लांब आहे? (kiti laamb aahe?)

one_ticket.note: Name the place first: पुण्याचं एक तिकीट द्या (Punyaacha ek ticket dya).

too_expensive.note: When bargaining, add: जरा कमी करा ना (jara kami kara na), 'bring it down a bit'.

cheaper.note: Also: जरा स्वस्त दाखवा (jara swast daakhva), 'show me something cheaper'.

id_like_this.note: Also common: मला हे पाहिजे (mala he paahije). At the counter: हे द्या (he dya).

just_looking.note: A woman says: मी फक्त बघतेय (mi fakt baghtey).

pay_card.note: Handy pattern for anything: कॅश चालेल का? (cash chaalel ka?), 'is cash OK?'

cash.note: In everyday speech कॅश (cash) is just as common.

open.note: In speech: दुकान चालू आहे (dukaan chaalu aahe), 'the shop is open'.

closed.note: Rhymes with 'fund'. Also means 'switched off', for lights, phones and so on.

big.note: With feminine nouns: मोठी (mothi); with neuter ones: मोठं (motha, with a light nasal).

small.note: Same form for every gender. Also common: छोटा (chhota).

good_evening.note: Formal or in messages. Face to face, people just say नमस्कार (namaskaar).

good_night.note: In everyday speech also गुड नाइट (good night).

see_you_later.note: Also: पुन्हा भेटू (punha bhetu), 'see you again'.

need_doctor.note: Also: डॉक्टरला बोलवा (doctorla bolva), 'please call a doctor'.

im_lost.note: A woman says: मी रस्ता चुकले आहे (mi rasta chukle aahe).

dont_feel_well.note: Also: माझी तब्येत बरी नाही (maajhi tabyet bari naahi).

pharmacy.note: In everyday speech people say मेडिकल (medical) or केमिस्ट (chemist).

hospital.note: In speech most say हॉस्पिटल (hospital). A local clinic is a दवाखाना (davaakhaana).

lost_phone.note: If it was stolen: माझा फोन चोरीला गेला (maajha phone chorila gela).

allergic.note: The allergen takes -ची: मला दुधाची ॲलर्जी आहे (mala dudhaachi allergy aahe), 'to milk'.

be_careful.note: Also: जपून! (japun!). Warning signs say सावधान (saavdhaan).

no_problem.note: Very common in speech: काही प्रॉब्लेम नाही (kaahi problem naahi).

of_course.note: More formal: अर्थात (arthaat). Also: हो, नक्की (ho, nakki).

i_like_it.note: For a lasting liking: मला हे आवडतं (mala he aavadta).

dont_like_it.note: For a lasting dislike: मला हे आवडत नाही (mala he aavadat naahi).

im_tired.note: A woman says: मी दमले आहे (mi damle aahe). Also common: थकलो / थकले (thaklo / thakle).

im_happy.note: Also: मला खूप आनंद झाला (mala khoop aanand jhaala), 'I'm delighted'.

welcome.note: Warm and usual at the door. Formal, for events and signs: स्वागत आहे (swaagat aahe).

my_family.note: In speech also: घरचे (gharche), 'the folks at home'.

mother.note: Also how you address her directly. Formal or literary: माता (maata).

father.note: Takes the respectful plural: माझे वडील (maajhe vadil). Calling him: बाबा (baaba).

brother.note: An elder brother is also called दादा (daada).

sister.note: An elder sister is also called ताई (taai).

child.note: Son: मुलगा (mulga); daughter: मुलगी (mulgi). Plural: मुलं (mula).

friend.note: A female friend: मैत्रीण (maitrin). Casual: दोस्त (dost).

this_is_my_friend.note: For a female friend: ही माझी मैत्रीण आहे (hi maajhi maitrin aahe).

are_you_married.note: Lit. 'Has your wedding taken place?' In speech often: झालंय का? (jhaalay ka?)

have_children.note: मुलं (mula) is the plural of मूल (mool), 'child'.

monday.note: -वार (-vaar) means 'day'. सोम (som) is the Moon: Moon-day, like Monday.

tuesday.note: मंगळ (mangal) is Mars. ळ is a retroflex l: curl the tongue back to say it.

saturday.note: शनि (shani) is Saturn: Saturn-day, like Saturday.

sunday.note: रवि (ravi) is the Sun: Sun-day, like Sunday.

weekend.note: The usual word today. The Marathi way: शनिवार-रविवार (shanivaar-ravivaar).

what_day.note: The answer: आज सोमवार आहे (aaj somvaar aahe).

next_week.note: As a noun ('next week is busy'): पुढचा आठवडा (pudhcha aathavda).

hundred.note: Marathi digits: १००. In bigger numbers it becomes -शे: एकशे दहा (ekshe daha), 110.

thousand.note: Marathi digits: १०००. Here ज sounds like 'dz': hadzaar.

how_old.note: वय (vay) means 'age'. Also common: तुमचं वय काय? (tumcha vay kaay?)

years_old.note: A woman says: मी … वर्षांची आहे (mi … varshaanchi aahe).

red.note: Same form for every gender. Also, more traditional: तांबडा (taambda).

blue.note: With feminine nouns: निळी (nili); with neuter ones: निळं (nila, with a light nasal).

what_colour.note: Also: हे कोणत्या रंगाचं आहे? (he kontya rangaacha aahe?)

this_one.note: For things in general. With a masculine noun: हा (ha); feminine: ही (hi). At the counter: हे द्या (he dya).

that_one.note: For things in general. With a masculine noun: तो (to); feminine: ती (ti).

another_one.note: Also: आणखी एक (aankhi ek). Add ना (na) to soften it: अजून एक द्या ना (ajun ek dya na).

its_hot.note: For sticky, humid heat: खूप उकडतंय (khoop ukadtay).

its_cold.note: If you feel cold: मला थंडी वाजतेय (mala thandi vaajtey).

its_raining.note: Lit. 'the rain is falling'. The monsoon season is पावसाळा (paavsaala).

its_sunny.note: ऊन (oon) is sunshine and the sun's heat: खूप ऊन आहे (khoop oon aahe), 'the sun is fierce'.

its_windy.note: Also: वारा सुटलाय (vaara sutlaay), 'the wind has picked up'.

weather_today.note: हवा (hava) means both air and weather. Forecasts say हवामान (havaamaan).

beautiful_day.note: About the weather itself: आज हवा छान आहे (aaj hava chhaan aahe).

umbrella.note: A must in the monsoon, roughly June to September.

summer.note: Roughly March to May, before the monsoon.

winter.note: Roughly November to February. The third season is पावसाळा (paavsaala), the monsoon.

have_reservation.note: Formal word, as on train tickets: आरक्षण (aarakshan).

room.note: In hotels people mostly say रूम (room).

check_out_time.note: किती वाजता (kiti vaajta) means 'at what time': works for trains, shops, anything.

map.note: On a phone most people just say मॅप (map).

bus.note: The red state-run intercity buses are called एसटी (ST).

next_train.note: Many say गाडी (gaadi) for a train. In Mumbai the suburban train is the लोकल (local).

is_this_seat_free.note: Also very natural: इथे कोणी बसलंय का? (ithe koni baslay ka?), 'is anyone sitting here?'

what_do_you_do.note: More specific: तुम्ही काय काम करता? (tumhi kaay kaam karta?)

i_work_in.note: A woman says: मी …मध्ये काम करते (mi …madhye kaam karte).

im_student.note: A woman says: मी विद्यार्थिनी आहे (mi vidyaarthini aahe).

im_busy.note: Lit. 'I'm in work'. Also common: मी बिझी आहे (mi busy aahe).

day_off.note: Also a holiday or vacation. 'I'm off today': आज मला सुट्टी आहे (aaj mala sutti aahe).

colleague.note: Same word for a woman, but 'my' changes: माझी सहकारी (maajhi sahakaari).

lets_start.note: चला (chala, said 'tsala'), 'come on', opens many 'let's…' phrases.

good_job.note: To a child or a junior: शाब्बास! (shaabbaas!)

table_for_two.note: Lit. 'Can we get a table for two people?' For four: चौघांसाठी (chaughaansaathi).

what_recommend.note: Lit. 'What's good here?' More formal: तुम्ही काय सुचवाल? (tumhi kaay suchvaal?)

not_spicy.note: Mild rather than none: कमी तिखट करा (kami tikhat kara).

vegetarian_food.note: Menus and signs say व्हेज (veg); meat dishes are नॉनव्हेज (non-veg).

more_water.note: Softer: जरा अजून पाणी द्या ना (jara ajun paani dya na).

no_sugar.note: Tea comes sweet unless you say so. Less sugar: साखर कमी (saakhar kami).

im_full.note: To refuse a second helping: नको, पुरे (nako, pure).

takeaway.note: In India takeaway food is called पार्सल (parcel).

it_was_delicious.note: Praising the cook: तुमच्या हाताला चव आहे (tumchya haataala chav aahe), 'your hand has taste'.

keep_change.note: Or wave it off with: राहू द्या (raahu dya), 'let it be'.

head.note: Ends in a light nasal sound, like मोठं (motha).

head_hurts.note: Works for any body part: माझा पाय दुखतोय (maajha paay dukhtoy), 'my leg hurts'.

have_fever.note: Lit. 'fever has come to me'. In speech: ताप आलाय (taap aalaay).

call_ambulance.note: Formal word: रुग्णवाहिका (rugnavaahika). Ambulance number in Maharashtra: 108.

need_rest.note: Also: मला आरामाची गरज आहे (mala aaraamaachi garaj aahe).

feel_better.note: बरं (bara) on its own also means 'OK, all right'.

get_well.note: To a woman: लवकर बऱ्या व्हा! (lavkar barya vha!) To a friend: लवकर बरा हो! (lavkar bara ho!)

lets_meet.note: Vaguer and very common: कधीतरी भेटूया (kadhitari bhetuya), 'let's meet sometime'.

are_you_free.note: Lit. 'Do you have time tomorrow?' Also: उद्या मोकळे आहात का? (udya mokle aahat ka?); to a woman: मोकळ्या (moklya).

call_me.note: Casual: मला फोन कर (mala phone kar).

your_number.note: Softer: तुमचा नंबर द्याल का? (tumcha number dyaal ka?), 'could I have your number?'

have_nice_day.note: Mostly written, e.g. in messages. In person many just say it in English.

good_luck.note: Lit. 'good wishes'. Before an exam or interview most people say ऑल द बेस्ट (all the best).

happy_birthday.note: Lit. 'heartfelt wishes on your birthday'. वाढदिवस (vaadhdivas) means 'growing day'.

thanks_a_lot.note: Also: तुमचे खूप आभार (tumche khoop aabhaar).

miss_you.note: Lit. 'your memory comes to me'. Right now: तुझी खूप आठवण येतेय (tujhi khoop aathvan yetey).
